name: Jeremiah
overview: Jeremiah was a male member of the tribe of Gad, noted as the tenth among the Gadites who joined David at Ziklag. His arrival at David's location is specifically mentioned, highlighting his role among those Gadites who aligned with David during that time.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeremiah means 'YHWH loosens [the womb]; YHWH lifts up; or possibly YHWH shoots, establishes.' This Hebrew name reflects a theophoric element invoking the Lord, though it was not given directly by God in this context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Jeremiah as a descendant of Gad, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Jeremiah's significance lies in his faithful commitment to David as one of the Gadite warriors, marking his place in the historical narrative of Israel's early monarchy. His presence at Ziklag with David situates him within the broader story of Israel's consolidation under David's leadership. This connection underscores the loyalty and support David received from various tribal groups during his rise to kingship.

keyEvents.event: Called by God as a youth
